problem_text:
A municipal water authority must devise a strategy to curtail total nutrient runoff from a network of agricultural drainage outlets. Initially, no mitigation practices are in place.

The characteristics of each drainage outlet are as follows:
* For Field 1, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 0.624, and the cultivated area is 135.478 hectares.
* For Field 2, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 1.837, and the cultivated area is 127.894 hectares.
* For Field 3, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 0.965, and the cultivated area is 249.866 hectares.
* For Field 4, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 0.756, and the cultivated area is 299.491 hectares.
* For Field 5, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 1.173, and the cultivated area is 165.921 hectares.
* For Field 6, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 2.288, and the cultivated area is 247.856 hectares.
* For Field 7, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 2.318, and the cultivated area is 132.562 hectares.
* For Field 8, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 1.082, and the cultivated area is 260.887 hectares.
* For Field 9, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 0.877, and the cultivated area is 287.911 hectares.
* For Field 10, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 1.734, and the cultivated area is 64.01 hectares.

To reduce nutrient loads, several best management practices (BMPs) are available, each with a specific capture efficiency:
* Implementing Practice1 will capture 28% of nutrients
* Implementing Practice2 will capture 84% of nutrients
* Implementing Practice3 will capture 52% of nutrients
* Implementing Practice4 will capture 75% of nutrients
* Implementing Practice5 will capture 23% of nutrients
* Implementing Practice6 will capture 25% of nutrients
* Implementing Practice7 will capture 24% of nutrients
* Implementing Practice8 will capture 80% of nutrients
* Implementing Practice9 will capture 29% of nutrients
* Implementing Practice10 will capture 70% of nutrients

Adopting a practice for a given field incurs an implementation cost per hectare of cultivated area. The cost matrix for all field–practice combinations is provided below:

| Field \ Practice | Practice1 | Practice2 | Practice3 | Practice4 | Practice5 | Practice6 | Practice7 | Practice8 | Practice9 | Practice10 |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Field 1 | 156.533 | 94.163 | 150.148 | 16.367 | 97.559 | 156.489 | 109.016 | 196.602 | 99.837 | 139.474 |
| Field 2 | 69.301 | 71.382 | 129.541 | 18.015 | 188.11 | 108.976 | 58.129 | 131.319 | 47.757 | 178.629 |
| Field 3 | 174.095 | 51.38 | 31.456 | 130.253 | 71.658 | 41.798 | 62.459 | 32.733 | 159.937 | 11.697 |
| Field 4 | 17.979 | 158.86 | 100.301 | 123.28 | 80.566 | 27.001 | 39.963 | 27.366 | 127.543 | 186.861 |
| Field 5 | 199.425 | 128.775 | 21.357 | 132.469 | 143.252 | 160.379 | 33.907 | 54.208 | 196.518 | 159.827 |
| Field 6 | 153.773 | 163.05 | 93.357 | 46.663 | 140.957 | 78.052 | 35.599 | 180.746 | 102.207 | 93.125 |
| Field 7 | 65.996 | 142.437 | 46.057 | 45.459 | 76.056 | 149.156 | 62.312 | 167.956 | 183.75 | 115.359 |
| Field 8 | 23.087 | 39.455 | 66.178 | 60.036 | 79.751 | 10.137 | 131.225 | 82.018 | 45.252 | 13.557 |
| Field 9 | 172.798 | 157.443 | 55.369 | 146.991 | 135.075 | 112.402 | 83.623 | 109.573 | 104.534 | 114.779 |
| Field 10 | 126.477 | 71.294 | 131.772 | 30.988 | 109.408 | 22.669 | 168.687 | 34.657 | 175.964 | 48.395 |

The authority must decide which practices to apply to each field (fields may adopt multiple practices concurrently), and a field may also remain partially untreated if needed. The objective is to guarantee that the total nutrient load is diminished by at least a proportion P = 0.443 of the baseline load, while minimizing the total implementation expenditure.
